title: Surjectivity of the affine-limit comparison implies local finite presentation for algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For every small nonempty directed set $I$, let $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of affine $S$-schemes with limit $T=\varprojlim_i T_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Suppose that for every such system the canonical map of sets
$$\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Mor}_S(T_i,X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,X)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Y)}\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Mor}_S(T_i,Y)$$
is surjective. Here the colimits are filtered colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and the maps to $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Y)$ are composition with $f$ and restriction to $T$. Then $f$ is locally of finite presentation: for every surjective etale scheme chart $V\to Y$ and every surjective etale scheme chart $U\to X\times_Y V$, the scheme morphism $U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or injectivity of the comparison map is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CM6 (lemma-surjection-is-enough); etale chart formulation: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03XP (definition-locally-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Fix arbitrary surjective etale scheme charts $g:V\to Y$ and $h:U\to Z=X\times_YV$. The sheaf fibre product $Z$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Write $r:U\to V$ and $q:U\to X$ for the projections of $h$. To test $r$, fix an inverse system of affine $V$-schemes $(T_i)$ with limit $T$, structural maps $b_i:T_i\to V$, and a $V$-map $a:T\to U$. These are also $S$-schemes and $S$-maps; put $x=q\circ a$ and denote the limit projections by $p_i$. Thus $f\circ x=g\circ b_i\circ p_i$.

source.place: Tag 0CM6 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), atlas reduction and two successive stage lifts.

proof.text: The pair $(x,[g\circ b_i])$ belongs to the fibre product in the hypothesis. Surjectivity supplies a class represented by $c_l:T_l\to X$ restricting to $x$, with $[f\circ c_l]=[g\circ b_i]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], choose a common later index $j\ge i,l$ where $f\circ c_j=g\circ b_j$. The pair $z_j=(c_j,b_j):T_j\to Z$ is therefore defined, and its restriction is exactly $h\circ a$, since both its $X$- and $V$-components agree.

source.place: Tag 0CM6 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), atlas reduction and two successive stage lifts.

proof.text: Form $E=T_j\times_ZU$. By [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], $E$ is a scheme and $e:E\to T_j$ is etale: it is the scheme test of the representable etale map $h$ along $z_j$. In particular $e$ is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The equality $z_j\circ p_j=h\circ a$ gives a $T_j$-map $s:T\to E$ with components $(p_j,a)$. No quasi-compactness of $E$ or $U$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0CM6 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), atlas reduction and two successive stage lifts.

proof.text: Use the tail $k\ge j$ as a system of affine $T_j$-schemes. Its limit is $T$, by the open-subscheme clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] with the open equal to all of $T_j$. The forward implication of [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion], applied to $e:E\to T_j$, and representatives from [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], descend $s$ to a $T_j$-map $s_k:T_k\to E$. Let $a_k:T_k\to U$ be its second projection. Then $a_k\circ p_k=a$ and $r\circ a_k=b_j\circ(T_k\to T_j)=b_k$. Thus the descended map is over $V$, not merely over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0CM6 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), atlas reduction and two successive stage lifts.

proof.text: For every affine inverse system over $V$, every $a\in\operatorname{Mor}_V(T,U)$ has now been lifted to a stage. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-surjective-affine-limit-criterion] with base $V$ to deduce that $r:U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation. The charts $V$ and $U$ were arbitrary, so this is exactly the chart condition asserted for $f$. Only surjectivity was used for $f$; the bijective scheme criterion in the preceding step was applied solely to the already etale morphism $E\to T_j$.

source.place: Tag 0CM6 (lemma-surjection-is-enough), atlas reduction and two successive stage lifts.
